if: the inward supply is a service of GENERAL INSURANCE, SERVICING, REPAIR OR MAINTENANCE
in so far as it relates to a motor vehicle, vessel or aircraft referred to in clause (a) or clause (aa)
AND the conveyance is not used for the purposes specified in those clauses
AND the recipient is not a taxable person engaged in manufacturing such conveyances or in supplying general insurance services in respect of such conveyances insured by him
then: input tax credit is NOT AVAILABLE on that service
note: The block follows the asset: if the conveyance is blocked, so is its insurance, servicing, repair and maintenance. Two escape routes exist — the conveyance being used for a purpose specified in clause (a) or (aa), or the recipient being a manufacturer of such conveyances or an insurer of them. Note the second route is defined by WHO receives the service, not by how the vehicle is used. Section 17(5) opens 'Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1) of section 16 and sub-section (1) of section 18', so this block defeats both the s.16(1) entitlement and the s.18(1) special-circumstances credit. Business use does not cure it. The source is the CGST Act as updated 31-08-2021. UNKNOWN whether a later amendment has changed this clause; later amendments are not held locally.
